title: How do we change paise into rupees?
description: Amounts in paise are written in rupees by moving the point two places left, and seventy-five paise is worked out step by step. Keeko's doubt is that five paise is zero point five rupees.
teaching_notes: One idea: a paisa is one hundredth of a rupee, so the point moves two places. Watch for students who forget the zero that holds the tenths place, and who drop the last zero of fifty paise.

source: Fill in the blanks (paise to rupees): 10 p, 5 p, 36 p, 50 p, 99 p, 250 p. Then write 75 paise in rupees, step by step.
video_script.why: The child has changed centimetres into metres and grams into kilograms and now changes money.
video_script.substitution: One paisa is one hundredth of a rupee, so the point moves two places when the unit changes.
video_script.anchor: a one rupee coin and the hundred paise it is worth
video_script.wrong_move: drops the zero that holds the empty tenths place
video_script.payoff_line: Paise to rupees moves the point two places left

final_answer.spoken: zero point seven five, zero point one zero, zero point zero five, zero point three six, zero point five zero, zero point nine nine and two point five zero rupees

video_script.fraction_reading: tenths and hundredths are said as words
maths_rules: 1 rupee = 100 paise, so 1 paisa = 1/100 rupee = Rs 0.01
the slip: Rs 0.5 is 50 paise, not 5 paise
video_script.design: The coin stays on the stage with its hundred paise; each amount slides to its place in the working band and the point moves two places. Keeko's doubt puts the five in the tenths place.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book, then a one rupee coin beside 100 paise; amounts 10 p, 5 p, 36 p, 50 p, 99 p, 250 p and 75 p; a question mark in the anchor band

marks.list: the amounts are written beside the coin
marks.ask: 75 p is marked to be worked step by step

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about changing paise into rupees.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Amounts such as ten paise, five paise and thirty-six paise are to be written in rupees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Seventy-five paise is also to be worked out step by step.

beats.on_screen: the amounts stay on the board; Keeko sits beside them as the child
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a one rupee coin cut into 100 equal paise; one paisa marked as 1/100 rupee = ₹0.01

marks.coin: the coin is cut into one hundred paise

narration: <bookmark mark='coin'/>A rupee has one hundred paise, so one paisa is one hundredth of a rupee.
<bookmark mark='hundredth'/>That is zero point zero one rupees.

beats.on_screen: Given: 10 p, 5 p, 36 p, 50 p, 99 p, 250 p and 75 p
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, ten, five, thirty-six, fifty, ninety-nine and two hundred fifty paise.
Also seventy-five paise, to be worked out in steps.

beats.on_screen: To find: each amount in rupees
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each amount in rupees.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 1 paisa = 1/100 rupee, so the point moves 2 places left

marks.move: an arrow shows the point moving two places left

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, one paisa is one hundredth of a rupee.
<bookmark mark='move'/>The point moves two places to the left.
<bookmark mark='p75'/>Step two, seventy-five paise is seventy-five hundredths of a rupee.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Seventy hundredths is seven tenths, so we get seven tenths plus five hundredths.
<bookmark mark='dec'/>That is zero point seven five rupees.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 10 p = ₹0.10; 5 p = ₹0.05, with a zero in the tenths place

marks.p5: 5 p is written with a zero in the tenths place as ₹0.05

narration: <bookmark mark='p10'/>Step three, ten paise is zero point one zero rupees.
<bookmark mark='p5'/>Five paise needs a zero in the tenths place, so it is zero point zero five rupees.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: 36 p = ₹0.36; 50 p = ₹0.50; 99 p = ₹0.99; 250 p = ₹2.50, which is 2 rupees and 50 paise

marks.p50: 50 p is written as ₹0.50 and 99 p as ₹0.99
marks.p250: 250 p is written as ₹2.50 and split into 2 rupees and 50 paise

narration: <bookmark mark='p36'/>Step four, thirty-six paise is zero point three six rupees.
<bookmark mark='p50'/>Fifty paise is zero point five zero rupees, and ninety-nine paise is zero point nine nine rupees.
<bookmark mark='p250'/>Two hundred fifty paise is two point five zero rupees, which is two rupees and fifty paise.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Paise to rupees moves the point two places left.
<bookmark mark='l1'/>Seventy-five paise is zero point seven five rupees, and ten paise is zero point one zero rupees.
<bookmark mark='l2'/>Five paise is zero point zero five rupees, and thirty-six paise is zero point three six rupees.
<bookmark mark='l3'/>Fifty paise is zero point five zero rupees, and ninety-nine paise is zero point nine nine rupees.
<bookmark mark='l4'/>Two hundred fifty paise is two point five zero rupees.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the coin
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 5 p = ₹0.5 appears and is struck out; the coin shows 5 of the 100 paise; ₹0.05 is written

marks.fix: ₹0.5 is struck out and 5 of the 100 paise are shaded
marks.zero: a zero is placed in the tenths place

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks five paise is zero point five rupees, because the five goes right after the point.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But one paisa is a hundredth of a rupee, so the five belongs in the hundredths place.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>The tenths place needs a zero, so five paise is zero point zero five rupees.
